focus: R29 LLM semantic filter on Pairs trading; PEAD enhancements; factor research; options strategies

items.title: RL for Speculative Trading under Exploratory Framework
items.relevance: R29 pairs trading — optimal OU-process entry/exit thresholds via RL. Closed-form Gibbs distribution for optimal intensity. Key: threshold depends on θ (mean reversion speed) and σ (spread volatility). High θ = tighter entry; low θ = wider threshold.

items.title: Anonymization and Information Loss (earnings call transcripts)
items.relevance: R31 implementation hazard — anonymizing transcripts destroys more signal than look-ahead bias. Company names, numbers, product/geo mentions carry the signal. EDGAR transcripts are public — no need to anonymize.

items.title: Asset allocation using a Markov process of clustered efficient frontier coefficients
items.relevance: R35 regime detection — third option alongside Wasserstein HMM and VIX/SMA. Detects regimes from portfolio behavior (EF coefficient shifts). Reproducible code available.

items.title: PolySwarm: Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Prediction Market Trading
items.relevance: Swarm of 50 LLM personas; KL/JS divergence to detect pair mispricings. Not directly applicable to equity pairs but methodology note.

items.title: The Co-Pricing Factor Zoo
items.relevance: Bayesian SDF factor averaging achieves OOS Sharpe 1.5-1.8. Factor aggregation > single factor models. Equity factors alone price bond risk premia. Background interest for R33 concept.

items.title: Advanced Deep Learning Techniques for Analyzing Earnings Call Transcripts
items.relevance: FinBERT 52% accuracy; Longformer 45%. 'Sugar-coated rhetoric' is a fundamental limitation. Confirms R31 design: use FinBERT domain-specific, focus on Q&A sections.
items.note: Confirms existing R31 decisions — no new actionable change

items.title: FinCall-Surprise: Multi-Modal Benchmark for Earnings Surprise Prediction
items.relevance: 26 LLMs tested on 2688 earnings calls. Class imbalance masks real accuracy. General LLMs struggle with financial nuance. Confirms: use domain-specific FinBERT not GPT/Claude for classification signal.
items.note: Confirms existing design; adds class imbalance warning — not new enough to stage

items.title: Not All Factors Crowd Equally — Alpha Decay paper
items.relevance: Hyperbolic alpha decay model. Key: crowding predicts tail risk, not alpha. Crowded reversal = higher crash probability. WITHDRAWN for insufficient empirical validation.
items.note: Paper withdrawn by author — do not rely on empirical results
